overview: The NRF24L01 is the go-to choice when a project needs cheap, low-power wireless communication between two or more microcontrollers — not phones, just other NRF24L01-equipped boards. It talks over SPI rather than the simpler UART used by Bluetooth or HC-12 modules, which gives it much higher throughput but a steeper setup curve, and it supports multi-node 'star' networks where one node can address several others by a configurable pipe address. Its onboard PCB trace antenna keeps range modest (tens of meters indoors); a version with an external antenna and power amplifier reaches much further at the cost of higher power draw.
simpleSummary: A cheap, low-power wireless module for sending data between two microcontrollers.

specifications.operatingVoltage: 1.9V - 3.6V (logic pins are 5V-tolerant on most breakouts, power rail is not)
specifications.range: ~10-100m depending on antenna variant and environment

pinMap.name: VCC
pinMap.currentLimit: ~12 mA average, spikes higher during transmit
pinMap.gotcha: Feeding 5V into VCC destroys the module immediately — this is a genuinely common mistake since the SPI logic pins nearby often ARE 5V tolerant, leading people to assume the power pin is too.

pinMap.name: CE
pinMap.function: Chip enable — toggles between standby and active TX/RX modes.

pinMap.name: IRQ
pinMap.function: Active-LOW interrupt output, signals events like data received or transmission complete.
pinMap.gotcha: Optional — many projects poll status registers over SPI instead of wiring this pin.

useCases.title: Wireless RC transmitter/receiver
useCases.scenario: Build a custom remote control for a car, drone, or robot with low latency and low power draw.

useCases.title: Multi-node sensor network
useCases.scenario: Several battery-powered sensor nodes reporting back to one central receiver.

oftenConfusedWith: HC-12 (simpler UART interface, longer range, lower throughput)
LoRa modules (much longer range, much lower data rate)
oftenUpgradedTo: LoRa modules when range matters more than data rate
